rows.answer: The paper describes the data used as follows: the Visual Genome (VG) training set consists of 85% of the data — 16k images and 740k corresponding region descriptions — while the ReferIt training data consists of 9k images and 54k referring expressions [6]. In addition, the instance selection model is trained using (region description, object set) pairs from the VG dataset, resulting in a training set of approximately 1.73M samples, with the remaining 300K samples split into validation and testing [4].

rows.answer: The paper presents results using precision, recall, and F$_1$. These are computed at the entity/content-element level by extracting all tagged spans for each content element type, deduplicating them, and comparing the resulting set against the ground truth using exact matches [1]. The results report F$_1$, precision, and recall, including metrics across all content elements (micro-averaged) and broken down by type [2]. For the data-efficiency analysis, the paper shows only F$_1$ scores, noting similar trends for the other metrics [3].
